title: Session concurrency and re-auth policy reconciliation for SSO (JIT + MFA)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood's SSO/SAML onboarding currently creates sessions via JIT provisioning but has inconsistent behavior across MFA-enforced tenants, admin-initiated logouts, and concurrent device sessions. This ticket specifies a reconciled session model that: binds sessions to SAML assertion IDs where available, defines explicit re-auth triggers for MFA step-up events, supports configurable concurrency limits, and surfaces audit events for every session lifecycle transition.

Goals:
- Define authoritative session binding semantics for SAML JIT sessions (assertion_id, authn_instant, audience) so revocation and logout propagation are reliable.
- Define default and tenant-configurable concurrency rules (per-user, per-tenant) and clear UX behavior for token refresh vs new session creation.
- Specify MFA expectation/step-up flows for sessions created without MFA or for tenants that upgrade to MFA after provisioning.
- Ensure every state change (create, refresh, step-up, logout, forced-revoke) emits structured audit logs with enough fields for compliance and incident forensics.
- Define admin override and revoke semantics consistent with RBAC v2 admin roles.

Scope (in-scope):
- SAML JIT provisioning session creation/metadata.
- Session token lifecycle (access/refresh/KV cache binding).
- MFA step-up policy enforcement and re-auth rules.
- Logout propagation (IdP-initiated, SP-initiated, admin revoke).
- Structured audit event schema additions.

Out-of-scope:
- Full UI changes for console (small to-be-created follow-up PM ticket).
- Legacy non-SAML session migrations (separate migration ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Every SAML JIT-created session stores assertion_id, authn_instant, issuer, nameid and tenant_id where present.

Default concurrency policy is configurable; default = 3 concurrent active sessions per user across devices. Concurrency enforcement should return 409 with well-documented retry semantics when exceeded.
MFA step-up requirement enforcement: when tenant policy requires MFA, existing non-MFA sessions must be marked as 'stepup_required' and expire within a configurable grace window (default 7 days).
IdP-initiated SLOs and SP-initiated logouts result in immediate session invalidation and an audit event (session.invalidate) with reason and originating_request_id.
Admin-initiated revokes by RBAC v2 admins include scope (user, tenant, device) and generate audit chain entries visible in Console and exported to SIEM.
All session lifecycle events conform to the audit schema v2 and include: event_id, timestamp, actor, target_session_id, assertion_id (if present), reason, and ip_address.
Integration tests covering: concurrent session creation up to limit, token refresh behavior post-MFA enforcement, idp-logout handling, and admin revoke replay to downstream systems (webhooks/stream).
design_considerations: Bind sessions to assertion_id when provided to make SLO atomic and enable deterministic logout propagation.
Use a configurable per-tenant concurrency policy with sensible global default rather than a hard-coded limit.
Grace window for MFA step-up aligns with product’s PLG flow to avoid customer friction; defaults must be conservative for regulated customers.
Audit payloads must be JSON-per-line compatible and avoid PII (mask nameid when tenant requests hashed identifiers).
Prefer soft-revoke mark (stepup_required) before hard expiry to enable UX-driven re-auth prompts without losing forensic visibility.
implementation_steps: API: extend session create response to include session.binding_info and concurrency_hint.
Runtime: persist assertion_id and authn_instant to session store (redis+postgres canonical mapping).
Policy: implement per-tenant concurrency lookup in auth middleware and return 409 with Retry-After when limit is reached.
MFA: implement background re-evaluation job that marks sessions as 'stepup_required' when tenant policy changes; emit audit events for state change.
Audit: update audit producer to include new session fields and publish to kafka topic audits.v2; add integration test to validate payload shape.
Admin UX/Control: add admin API endpoints for scoped revoke (user/tenant/device) that check RBAC v2 roles and emit an audit chain entry.
E2E: add tests for IdP-initiated logout handshake simulation and ensure session invalidation is idempotent.
Docs: update developer docs with error semantics (409 on concurrency), audit schema, and migration notes for early adopters.
discussion: 2025-02-12 — Luis: Proposed default concurrency 3 to balance PLG and security. Concern: higher memory usage for session store. (commented: need capacity estimate)
2025-02-14 — Priya (PM): Regulation customers should be allowed to set 1 as policy; add tenant-level override. (agreed)
2025-02-18 — Ben (Security): Audit schema must not contain raw nameid for EU tenants; recommend hashing with tenant salt. (action: add mask option)
2025-02-21 — Design: Console needs small indicator when session is 'stepup_required' vs active; we'll sketch in follow-up ticket.
decisions: Use assertion_id binding where present; fall back to ephemeral session id when missing.
Default concurrency = 3; tenant-configurable down to 1 and up to 10 via admin policy.
MFA enforcement uses 'stepup_required' flag with default grace window 7 days; can be shortened to 0 for strict tenants.
Audit payloads will include hashed_nameid when tenant requests PII minimization; implement tenant salt rotation support.
risks_mitigations: Increased session metadata will grow storage footprint — mitigation: TTLs and compact audit payloads; add retention policy for session audit events.
Race during concurrent session creation — mitigation: atomic increment in redis and compensate on failure with cleanup job.
Misconfigured tenant policies could lock users out — mitigation: add admin 'emergency_grant' endpoint guarded by RBAC v2 and audit.
